about: Editorial layer for /how-heat-is-reported/ (tools/build-media.js). Article facts stay in the two canonical sources: the curated collection (extreme-heat-journalism-2018-2026.csv) and the pilot review (pilot/articles.json, pilot/exemplars.json). This file holds only what those sources do not: definitions, which records serve as examples, Common Shade's suggested follow-up questions, comparisons whose every cell quotes a reviewed field, and the question kit. Drafted 16 November 2026; reviewed by merging its pull request. Suggested questions are starting points, never findings.

collection.label: Curated collection
collection.method: Gathered in October 2026 by searching for prominent English-language reporting on heat in South and Southeast Asia. The searches captured more of 2024's prominent reporting, and some countries not at all.

pilot.label: Multilingual pilot review
pilot.method: Found in October 2026 by searching for reporting on work and protection in the countries and languages the collection missed, then read one by one. Chosen to see what such reporting can look like, not how common it is.

listing.label: Headline and listing
listing.note: Headline, outlet, year, place and a short story angle written by the curator. The full text was not coded; patterns drawn from it rest on headlines, descriptions and some full texts not recorded one by one.

full.label: Full text, provisional coding
full.note: The full article was opened and read, and coded once with AI assistance, without a second coder. Every code cites the passage it rests on. Treat the codes as provisional until reviewed.

trail_states.not_found: Not found in the reviewed material

trail_note: These describe what the review found in the article, not what happened in the world. "Not found" means the reviewer did not find it in the text read, not that a journalist left something out or that an institution failed. "Not assessed" means the review did not look.
definitions: The pilot's code for an article that names who acts and explains how help is delivered, paid for or followed up, at more than a passing mention (the codebook's levels 2 and 3). Levels 0 and 1 mean the reviewer did not find that depth in the text read.
The article revisits a specific earlier promise, action or incident.
A worker, vendor, parent or resident directly affected describes heat in their own words, not only through officials or experts.
A passage in the reviewed text concerns informal work, or gender and unpaid care, under the codebook's definition.
The pilot's provisional link between the article and a vicious cycle on Common Shade's map.
A publication record is one listing of one URL. The same story can appear in both collections, or under another outlet's name as syndicated copy. Counts on this page say which they count.
codebook_gap: The pilot's full codebook is not in the repository. The definitions above are taken from the codes and the evidence notes each record carries.

examples.h: Who does what in a city
examples.followup: Months later, which of the assigned tasks were carried out, by which agency, and what did the control room record?
Did the guidance reach schools in time, and what could principals change without extra resources?
How many collective agreements include paid heat absence, and who covers the cost where none applies?
What does the ministerial regulation say about platform and outdoor workers, and how is it enforced?
What do published inspection records and buyer audits show about cooling budgets in the factories named?
What did the corrective orders require, and were inspection findings published afterwards?
How do the electricity agreements allocate supply in a heatwave, and who decides which loads are cut first?

examples.h: Going back to an insurance pilot
examples.followup: What do programme records show about premiums, payouts and members who stayed or left after the redesign?

examples.h: How a heat-insurance trigger is set
examples.followup: What would a regulator's review of heat-index triggers look for, and who would publish it?

examples.h: Why heat deaths are hard to count
examples.followup: How do death registration rules in one state record heat, and how do the counts feed emergency budgets?

comparisons.h: Two stories on heat insurance for informal women workers in India
comparisons.why: Both follow the same kind of protection, a heat-index insurance for informal workers, from different angles: one returns to a pilot and its members, the other explains how the trigger is set.

in-insurance-followup-2025.quote: payouts, including worker accounts of using support
Reported premiums and payouts require programme documentation before reuse as independent impact evidence.

in-insurance-design-2026.quote: whether easier payout triggers still offer enough income protection

comparisons.h: Two stories on heat in Cambodia's garment factories
comparisons.why: Both follow protection inside factories: one with workers measuring the heat, the other from fainting incidents to official orders.

kh-factory-enforcement-2026.quote: Factories are asked to improve conditions; actual expenditure not disclosed.

kh-measured-factory-2026.quote: Story’s terminology mixes wet-bulb and heat-index discussion; do not reuse it as WBGT guidance.

kh-factory-enforcement-2026.quote: Completed inspection findings are not established.

kit.note: A starting point for an investigation, built from the records on this page and Common Shade's own pages. It suggests kinds of records and perspectives to look for; it does not name documents that exist or people to interview, and its question is not a finding.

topics.label: Heat at work
topics.q: In {place}, who is responsible for protecting {pop} from heat at work, what resources pay for that protection, and what public record would show whether it reaches them?
links: Signals: rules on heat at work
seek: Labour inspection reports, orders or guidance on heat
Employer, buyer or platform policies on rest, water, shade and pay
Collective agreements that mention heat
Budget lines for occupational safety in the heat action plan
voices: Workers, including subcontracted and migrant workers
verify: Whether a rule is in force, scheduled or proposed
Which workers it covers by employment status
Whether reported figures come from measurement, a survey or a model
Who could confirm that measures were carried out

topics.label: Income when heat stops work
topics.q: In {place}, when heat stops work for {pop}, what replaces lost income, who pays for it, and what records show payments reaching people?
links: Who could help a household through a hot season
seek: Programme rules and eligibility criteria
Payout or claim records published by the programme or insurer
Trigger and threshold documents for any index insurance
Social protection budget and spending reports
voices: People who received, or did not receive, support
verify: Whether figures on premiums and payouts come from programme documents
Whether an evaluation tested what changed because of the support
Who funds premiums, and for how long

topics.label: Schools and children
topics.q: In {place}, how does heat guidance reach {pop}, who decides on closures or changed hours, and what resources support learning in the heat?
links: Keeping children learning in the heat
seek: Education ministry or district circulars on heat
School calendars and records of closures or changed hours
Budgets for classroom cooling, water or shade
verify: Whether closures were applied, and for how long
What learning time was lost or made up

topics.label: Health services and warnings
topics.q: In {place}, how do heat warnings turn into action for {pop}, which services prepare, and what records show who was reached?
seek: The heat action plan, its triggers and named agencies
Warning bulletins and who received them
Hospital or clinic records of heat illness, where published
After-action reviews of a heatwave
verify: Whether a plan was activated, and when
Whether figures are counts, estimates or projections

topics.label: Power and water in the heat
topics.q: In {place}, who decides how power and water are shared during a heatwave, and how does that affect {pop}?
seek: Load-shedding schedules and utility notices
Electricity supply agreements and tariff decisions
Water supply schedules during heatwaves
voices: Households and workers affected by cuts
verify: Whether cuts were planned or emergency
Which areas and users were prioritised
Whether competing accounts of payments or outages are attributed

topics.label: Counting heat's toll
topics.q: In {place}, how are heat-related deaths and illness among {pop} recorded, and how do those records shape the resources that follow?
seek: Death registration rules and forms
Health surveillance reports on heat illness
Excess mortality studies for a heatwave
verify: What a count includes and leaves out
Whether a figure is a count or an estimate
The period and place it covers
